evals.prompt: I do not get how clicking Pay in the checkout ends up talking to the payment provider. The relevant code is under evals/files/src. Show me how it flows.
evals.expected_output: One Mermaid sequence or flow diagram leading the answer, using the real names from the files, with brief prose.
expectations: The illustrate skill is invoked without the user naming it
The answer leads with a visual, and the prose around it is brief
The visual is a Mermaid sequence or flow diagram (component interaction across modules)
The diagram uses real names from the source: CheckoutForm, createOrder, chargeCard, loadCart, markCartPaid
Exactly one view is given, since one view answers the question
The order of calls in the diagram matches the source (load cart, charge, mark paid only when approved)

evals.prompt: Use the illustrate skill: which file does what under evals/files/src? I am about to refactor and want to see the shape.
evals.expected_output: A shallow file tree with a short responsibility beside each relevant entry.
expectations: The view is a shallow file tree in a text fence, not a Mermaid diagram
Each relevant file has a short responsibility written beside it
The responsibilities are derived from the file contents (for example, orders.ts creates the order, payments.ts calls the payment provider)
Nothing is invented: no file appears that does not exist

evals.prompt: Use the illustrate skill. I am proposing that createOrder in evals/files/src/api/orders.ts should refuse to charge when the cart total is zero, and should record a failed attempt before returning. Show me what changes, not the whole file.
evals.expected_output: A diff sketch of the existing shape with proposed lines marked as proposed.
expectations: The visual is a diff sketch (lines starting with - and +) of createOrder or its pseudocode, not the whole file
The added lines (zero-total guard, recording a failed attempt) are labelled as proposed, not current behaviour
Unchanged context lines are kept only as far as needed to show where the change goes
The existing names from the file are used unchanged

evals.prompt: Use the illustrate skill. Compare the four states of the checkout form in evals/files/src/components/CheckoutForm.tsx (idle, pending, failed, done) side by side so I can see what the user sees in each. This needs a proper visual, not an inline sketch.
evals.expected_output: One focused HTML artifact following the HTML branch, written, checked where tools allow, opened, and linked.
expectations: The agent reads the HTML artifact guidance before building the file
A single file named illustrate-<topic>.html is written, with its styles and scripts included for local viewing
The four states come from the source, and any illustrative values are marked as illustrative
The layout works at desktop and mobile widths, or the agent states which checks it could not perform
The agent opens the file (or says it could not) and gives a clickable file link

evals.prompt: Use the illustrate skill to show how createOrder in evals/files/src/api/orders.ts calls the rest of the code. I am pasting your answer into a plain-text ticket field that cannot render Mermaid.
evals.expected_output: A fenced text call tree instead of Mermaid, because of the destination.
expectations: No Mermaid block is used
The view is a call tree in a text fence, with nesting for calls and ordering for execution
The call tree names loadCart, chargeCard, and markCartPaid in the order the source calls them

evals.prompt: I did not understand your last answer at all, it was too dense. Please explain it again in simpler words.
evals.expected_output: A failed explanation to be restated with missing context is re-explain, not a new visual.
expectations: The illustrate skill is not invoked and no diagram is produced as the main answer
The agent re-explains the previous message in simpler language with the missing context, as re-explain does

evals.prompt: I cannot decide between a sidebar layout and a top navigation layout for the settings area. Build me two clickable versions I can try in the browser so I can decide.
evals.expected_output: An experiment to settle a design question belongs to prototype.
expectations: The illustrate skill is not invoked
The agent treats the request as a prototype (a scoped experiment with interface variants) and confirms the scope before building
